title: Every charger is a computer
text: Every public E V charger is a networked computer. It reports to a management system, the C S M S, usually over the site's shared wifi. That link is what attackers go after.

title: The leak
text: A published system claimed ninety-eight percent accuracy on this problem. We reproduced it and found a leak: one timestamp column alone scores ninety-nine point eight percent. The model was recognising the recording, not the attack.

title: Why F1, not accuracy
text: Why we report F1, not accuracy. After removing duplicates, floods make up over eighty percent of the flows, and ninety-nine percent on the published feature set. A model that gets the floods right and misses every scan still scores high accuracy: on that published set, accuracy is ninety-nine point six percent, while macro F1 is only zero point seven. Macro F1 scores each of the fifteen traffic classes separately and averages them, so a missed scan counts as much as a flood. With the leak removed, macro F1 is about zero point five five. That is the honest number.

title: Floods vs scans
text: That average hides two very different results. Floods are named ninety-nine point eight percent of the time. The six scan types sit near zero point two F1 each, because at the flow level they look almost identical.

title: Scans are recognised, rarely named
text: Ninety-six percent of scans are still recognised as scans, even though only thirty-four percent get the exact scan name. X G Boost is our primary detector, with the fewest false alarms on normal traffic: one point eight percent.

title: Close the loop
text: Sentinel watches a mirrored copy of the site's traffic. But detection alone doesn't stop anyone. So we close the loop: detect, contain, harden, verify.

title: Flood: quarantine
text: Floods are named reliably, so Sentinel recommends quarantining that one device at the switch. An operator approves it, the attack traffic stops, and the chargers stay online.

title: Scan: restrict, then escalate
text: Scans are often misnamed, so the response is softer. The device keeps internet access, but can no longer reach the chargers, and it is now watched. When that same laptop starts flooding, it is quarantined on its very first flood flow.

title: Compromised car: stop the session
text: A compromised car attacks through the charging cable, so the charger ends the session and blocks the car. That can only happen while charging. When the station is idle, there is no car to attack from.

title: Harden
text: Then each role hardens the site so the same attack fails next time: S Y N cookies and rate limits, stations that answer only the C S M S, and chargers that accept only charging messages from the car.

title: Replayed: 20 of 20 contained
text: We replayed every recorded attack through this loop. Twenty out of twenty were contained, with no actions on normal traffic. Sentinel recommends. A person approves every action.
